explanations.explanation: That's the first challenge, baker. The LORD says, “Let them come and tell us what will happen.” (Isaiah 41:22) He wants a prediction, something that can be checked once the day comes. Nobody can fake that one for long.

Nice try, friend, but nobody gets to brag in this courtroom. The LORD never asks the idols for a speech about how strong they are. He says, “Let them come and tell us what will happen.” (Isaiah 41:22) Talk is cheap, and He wants something that can be checked.

Reading out a rulebook sounds official, I'll give you that. But the LORD doesn't ask for laws at all. He asks them to “…tell us what will happen.” and to “Tell the former things…” too. (Isaiah 41:22) The test is about what they can tell, both what's past and what's coming.

Right, baker. The LORD says, “Tell the former things, so that we may reflect on them and know the outcome.” (Isaiah 41:22) Then He adds, “Or announce to us what is coming.” So the idols have two ways to answer, the past or the future, and they can't do either.

I get why you'd think it was only the future, friend. But the verse has more. The LORD says, “Tell the former things, so that we may reflect on them and know the outcome.” (Isaiah 41:22) After that comes “Or announce to us what is coming.” so the past and the future are both on the table.

You got it, baker. The LORD says, “Tell us the things that are to come, so that we may know that you are gods.” (Isaiah 41:23) That's the whole point of the trial. If they can't pass this, the claim doesn't hold.

Big claim, friend, but the LORD doesn't put it on the table. He says the things to come would let us “…know that you are gods.” (Isaiah 41:23) The test is about telling what's coming, not about who made what.

Ooh, that one's close to the courtroom, but it's not in the verse. Here the LORD is called “…the King of Jacob.” (Isaiah 41:21) What the idols' answer would show is stated in verse 23: “…that you are gods.”
That's the verdict, baker. The LORD says, “Behold, you are nothing and your work is of no value.” (Isaiah 41:24) Plain and short. I've heard longer rulings on a burnt batch.
Mighty? Friend, that's the exact opposite of what He says. The LORD tells the idols, “Behold, you are nothing and your work is of no value.” (Isaiah 41:24) Nothing mighty about nothing.

Being old doesn't help them in this courtroom, friend. A thing can be around for ages and still count for nothing. The LORD says, “Behold, you are nothing and your work is of no value.” (Isaiah 41:24)

I see why you'd say that, friend, but the verdict keeps going. After calling the idols nothing, the LORD says, “Anyone who chooses you is detestable.” (Isaiah 41:24) So it reaches the people who choose them too, and that makes this statement false.
That's right, baker. The verdict isn't only about the idols. The LORD says, “Anyone who chooses you is detestable.” (Isaiah 41:24) It reaches the ones who pick them, and that's a serious line.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, “I have raised up one from the north, and he has come—one from the east who calls on My name.” (Isaiah 41:25) He names both directions. I couldn't tell you why both, because the verse doesn't say.
Not quite, friend, and I've gotten turned around in a dark drawer myself, so I feel you. The verse says “…from the north…” and “…from the east…” (Isaiah 41:25) South and west don't show up at all.

Good guess if you like scenery, but the verse deals in directions. The LORD says, “I have raised up one from the north, and he has come—one from the east who calls on My name.” (Isaiah 41:25) No sea and no desert are mentioned.

Yes, baker. The LORD says it plainly: “…one from the east who calls on My name.” (Isaiah 41:25) The one He raised up is the one calling on His name. That's the detail the statement asks about, and you caught it.
Careful, friend, the verse says the opposite. The LORD describes “…one from the east who calls on My name.” (Isaiah 41:25) So this one does call on His name, which makes the statement true.
Not one, baker. The LORD says, “No one announced it, no one foretold it, no one heard your words.” (Isaiah 41:26) Zero for the whole lineup, and that was the test.

Nobody gets to be the wise old exception here, friend. The LORD says, “No one announced it, no one foretold it, no one heard your words.” (Isaiah 41:26) The verse names no oldest one, and none of them spoke up.
A whole chorus, friend? I'd love to see that. But the LORD says, “No one announced it, no one foretold it, no one heard your words.” (Isaiah 41:26) The whole group came up empty.
That's it, baker. The LORD says, “…I gave to Jerusalem a herald of good news.” (Isaiah 41:27) A herald is someone who brings word, and here the word is good news.

explanations.answer: A new king on the throne
explanations.explanation: A king would make a big entrance, I'll grant you. But the verse says something else. The LORD says, “…I gave to Jerusalem a herald of good news.” (Isaiah 41:27) No new king is mentioned.

explanations.answer: A wall of fire around it
explanations.explanation: Dramatic, friend, and I like the energy. But that's not in these verses. The LORD says, “…I gave to Jerusalem a herald of good news.” (Isaiah 41:27) That's the gift, and no wall of fire appears.
True, baker. The LORD says, “when I ask them, they have nothing to say.” (Isaiah 41:28) He asks, and the idols give Him silence. I've had a quiet oven act more helpful than that.
Easy one to flip, friend, but the verse is clear. The LORD says, “when I ask them, they have nothing to say.” (Isaiah 41:28) The idols stay silent. So the statement is true.

That's the word, baker. The LORD says, “See, they are all a delusion; their works amount to nothing; their images are as empty as the wind.” (Isaiah 41:29) He calls the idols a delusion, and He says their images are as empty as the wind.
A secret would mean something hidden that's worth knowing. That's not what He says. The LORD says, “See, they are all a delusion…” (Isaiah 41:29) Nothing hidden here, friend.
A rumor at least gets people talking, friend. But the LORD uses a different word. He says, “See, they are all a delusion; their works amount to nothing…” (Isaiah 41:29) The word is delusion.
